items.name: Readability
items.evidence: The code is mostly clear and the public methods have doc comments. But single-letter names like `p := new(Polygon)`, `s`, `e` and `d` are used throughout the business logic. The long Decode body has very few inline comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: ShapeIndex.Decode is one function of roughly 170 lines (cap: bad), and Encode is about 100 lines. Both use near-identical, copy-pasted type switches per tag. The code went into shapeindex.go instead of the requested dedicated shapeindex_encode.go.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Counts are bounded, but the caps of 100000000 still allow huge allocations (`make([]CellID, numCells)`). Converting a huge uvarint with `int(edgeID)` can go negative and get past the `>= numShapeEdges` check. It reads maxEdgesPerCell before checking d.err and uses the magic number 1000000. Loop/LaxLoop are not supported.

items.name: Existing encodings and Shape interface unchanged
items.name_zh: 既有编码格式与 Shape 接口不变
items.evidence: The new methods are additive, and existing typeTag values and wire formats are unchanged. One incidental change: the internal `Polyline.decode(d decoder)` became `decode(d *decoder)`, with no format impact. No tags were added for Loop/LaxLoop, so those types still cannot be encoded.
